issue: दुःख निर्गुण नाशन हारे हो — both witnesses (the book and Drik Panchang) print निर्गुण; 'destroyer of sorrow and of the nirguṇa' hardly makes sense, and दुर्गुण (vice) would. An independent witness, Mukesh's 1950 recording of this prayer (transcribed on Atul's Song A Day, atulsongaday.me, 'Pitu maatu sahaayak swaami sakha'), sings durgun; the text (not the meaning) is where it would be corrected, so the meaning follows the printed word until the text is settled.
our reading: दुःख निर्गुण नाशन हारे हो (as printed), read: you, beyond all qualities (निर्गुण), are the destroyer of sorrow

issue: भुलि हैं हम तो तुमको — the half-line is three syllables shorter than the other first halves (पितु मातु सहायक स्वामी सखा, उपकारन को कछु अन्त नहीं), so a word may be missing; both witnesses agree. No independent web source found.
our reading: भुलि हैं हम तो तुमको (as printed)
alternatives: a fuller form (e.g. with गये / भले) not attested in our witnesses

issue: मुझसे बिरले बुधवारे हो — the sense is unclear (बुधवारे: 'the wise'? 'मुझसे' with बिरले is odd); both witnesses agree.
our reading: as printed, read: rarely found by the likes of me (मुझसे बिरले), you belong to the wise (बुधवारे)
alternatives: समुझे बिरले बुधवारे हो (only a rare wise man understands it), a likely misprint of समुझे as मुझसे; not attested in our witnesses
